candidates.change_summary: Change the value requirement from 10 ether to 5 ether.
Delete the timestamp guard require(block.timestamp > pastBlockTime).
Store block.timestamp instead of block.timestamp + 1 in pastBlockTime.
Delete the statement that updates pastBlockTime.
Invert the payout condition from block.number % 15 == 0 to block.number % 15 != 0.
Delete the statement that updates pastBlockTime, so it never changes value.
Replace the pastBlockTime update with block.timestamp instead of block.timestamp + 1.
Relax the guard to >=, allowing calls within the same timestamp to succeed where P reverts.
Relax the timestamp guard from strictly greater to greater-or-equal, allowing a call in the immediately next timestamp window.
Record the current timestamp instead of timestamp + 1, permitting an earlier subsequent successful call.
Delete the update of pastBlockTime so the one-call-per-timestamp restriction is never enforced after the first call.
Invert the modulo condition so payouts occur on blocks not divisible by 15 instead of those divisible by 15.
Delete the payout transfer so no funds are ever sent to the caller.
Change the required deposit from 10 ether to 1 ether so calls with 10 ether revert and calls with 1 ether succeed.
Delete the statement `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp + 1;` so pastBlockTime is never updated.
Replace the assignment with `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` so the stored value is the timestamp itself.
Replace the assignment with `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp + 2;` so a different value is stored.
